stem.en: A gardener grows twenty roses from cuttings of one bush and twenty from seeds of the same bush. What should she expect?

text.en: The cuttings will be weaker, because they began with no roots.

feedback.en: A cutting grows its own roots from the stem. It is not a weaker kind of plant.

text.en: The seed plants will all match the parent exactly.

feedback.en: Seeds come from sexual reproduction, so the young get a mix of characters and can differ.

text.en: The cuttings will match the bush; seed plants may differ.

feedback.en: Yes. Cuttings have one parent and are genetically identical to it. Seed plants carry a mix.

text.en: The cuttings will differ, as each grows its own roots.

feedback.en: Growing new roots does not change what a cutting carries from its parent.

explanation.en: A cutting has one parent, so it is genetically identical to that parent. A seed plant gets a mix of characters from two parents, so seed plants can differ from one another.

hints.en: Count the parents in each case.
New roots come from the stem itself. Does that change what the plant carries?
